bull.b: Multiple products are showing strong prescription, unit, and prescriber growth, indicating broadening adoption rather than reliance on a single franchise. Continued traction across dry eye and surgical therapies can support durable revenue expansion and improve commercial leverage over the next several quarters.

bull.t: High gross margins and improving cash generation
bull.b: Positive operating and free cash flow represent a meaningful improvement from prior periods and provide internal funding for commercial investment. Combined with very high gross margins, this supports the potential for stronger earnings conversion if revenue growth persists and operating costs become more disciplined.

bull.t: Expanding ophthalmic portfolio and market access
bull.b: Adding TYRVAYA broadens Harrow’s dry-eye offering with a complementary delivery format, while expanded PBM coverage can increase the addressable patient base for VEVYE. A wider portfolio and improved access may strengthen physician coverage and support sustained commercial productivity.

bear.t: Elevated leverage and thin equity cushion
bear.b: Higher debt alongside a sharply reduced equity base limits financial flexibility and makes the company more sensitive to execution shortfalls or weaker operating performance. The resulting refinancing and dilution risks could constrain investment capacity and absorb cash that might otherwise support growth.

Strong product economics have not yet translated into dependable bottom-line profitability, indicating that operating costs or other headwinds are absorbing much of the gross profit. Persistent losses could limit self-funded expansion and make sustainable earnings dependent on successful cost and integration execution.

The reimbursement change removes an important channel for IHEEZO and restricts uptake in ambulatory surgical centers, requiring greater reliance on in-office markets. This can limit near-term addressable demand, complicate commercialization, and make revenue growth more dependent on successful channel repositioning.
